A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ring-attractor reinforcement-learning work. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and retained text, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ring-attractor experiments on Mario, Highway and Atari, including implemented EffZero/EffZeroRA results and topology ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a continuous-action Highway evaluation and weight-evolution analyses.

M1.justification: The two main approaches remain, but the written neuron dynamics change: v1 Eqs. 2–3 divide both drive and leak by tau, whereas v2 divides only the drive; the full inhibitory update changes similarly. This revises the specified procedure, although the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun. The SNN-to-CTRNN renaming alone is not a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds a continuous one-dimensional circular-action Highway evaluation for exogenous BDQN variants (Figure 2 and Table 2), alongside the retained discrete Highway DL evaluation. Mario and the same 19 Atari games remain covered.

E2.justification: The retained BDQN, DQN/DDQN and CURL/SPR/EffZero comparisons preserve their comparator membership. The added Highway experiment extends the existing BDQN/BDQNRA/BDQNRA-UA comparison from Mario to another scenario, without introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: The new weight-evolution study trains both input-to-hidden and hidden-to-hidden connections and examines checkpoints at 0, 300,000, 600,000 and 1,000,000 steps. This introduces an experimental variant of the standard fixed-input-weight model. The retained Atari evaluation still uses 100,000 environment steps.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2.3 adds a focused analysis of whether ring connectivity persists when both weight matrices are trainable, illustrated in Figures 6–7. The existing randomized-action and removed-circular-weight ablations are retained as A.2.1–A.2.2.

E5.justification: Learning curves retain ten-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting, and Table 1 retains ten seeds with three samples per seed. New results also use mean/SD displays; no new repeated-run policy, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The new Highway panel reports BDQNRA-UA performing best, followed by BDQNRA and BDQN. Figures 6–7 add findings that input weights preserve distance-dependent structure while recurrent weights develop different patterns. Every Table 1 cell and all previously reported performance and ablation plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the recurrent wraparound distance in Eq. 12, changing v1 Eq. 13's N - |m - m| term to N - |m - n|, alongside the dynamics revisions. Appendix A.4 adds neutral-action distance and coupled-ring definitions and sketches dense O(R²) versus sparse O(R) complexity. These extend the mathematical specification without adding a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions of spatially structured action selection, Bayesian uncertainty handling and a reusable DL ring-attractor module. The headline claim of a 53% Atari performance improvement is also retained.

C2.justification: A.2.3 newly interprets preserved input connectivity and adaptable recurrent connectivity as support for the standard fixed-input/trainable-recurrent design. Section 4.2 replaces v1's misleading account of BLR uncertainty evaluation with an explanation of the DDQNRA comparison. Existing high-dimensional and less-spatial applicability concerns remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation disclosure: Algorithm 1, fixed versus trainable connection information, neutral-action handling, multi-ring coupling initialized at kappa = 0.1, and Table 2's environment-specific action and ring configurations. It also adds a codebase link. Much of this documents implementations already represented in v1 rather than establishing new experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references on CTRNNs, Bayesian ring attractors and biological navigation, including Beer, Kutschireiter et al., Singh et al., Wilson, and Xiong and Sridhar. It removes the Foerster et al. Bayesian action-decoder discussion. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution wording and Section 4.2 are edited; SNN terminology becomes CTRNN; future work becomes a separate section; and appendix headings are reorganized. Much of the prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, substantially resizing and repositioning existing displays. Figure 2 gains a Highway panel, Figure 3's panels are stacked, and Algorithm 1, Figures 6–7 and Table 2 are added. The original RNN schematic is retained as Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the implementation easier to inspect, corrects Section 4.2's explanation and adds focused empirical support while retaining the principal Atari evidence. These provide a limited overall improvement. Incorrect equation references in Algorithm 1 and the compressed presentation of Table 1 reduce the benefit.
